**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Test more than the exposed 0.5 scale**

Because the only candidate-visible case always supplies `value_scale = 0.5`, an implementation that uses a constant 0.5 whenever `attention_value_scale` is present will match both golden outputs and pass while producing incorrect results for every other configured scale. Add multiple distinct scale cases so this grader establishes that the configuration value itself is honored.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L48-L48](https://github.com/mitukx/VARE/blob/a892e39b6baa746b63e4ab2133039b09b958be4a/AGENTS.md#L48-L48)

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Exercise the cache path before accepting patches**

Both oracle calls run a cache-free full forward, so a patch that applies the scale after attention (or after the bias-free output projection) produces the same tensors and passes even though it leaves cached values unscaled, contrary to the task's required pre-cache placement. Include incremental calls with `make_cache()` and verify the resulting cached-generation behavior so such patches cannot count as successful.

In a fresh checkout, this documented command fails before calibration because the committed `results/mlxlm-1971-isolated-v3/run-1` directory already exists while `main()` calls `output.mkdir(..., exist_ok=False)`. **<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Include all versioned task modules in the audit inventory**

When a continuation campaign runs from the current tree, `scripts/benchmark_e2e_rl_continuation.py` snapshots every Python file under `src/vare`—now 81 files—but this inventory adds only the base #1971 module and omits `mlxlm_1971_repo_task_v2.py`, `_v3.py`, and `_v4.py`. **<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Require semantic mismatches from negative controls**

If the baseline or either mutant times out, crashes during import, or emits malformed output, its report still has `passed == False`, so this predicate can declare the calibration successful as long as the known fix and red-team checks pass. That does not demonstrate that the grader distinguishes the intended value-scale defects; require the expected per-case pattern, including `wrong_output` failures and the constant mutant's passing 0.5 case, rather than accepting any failure mode.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Use a fresh output path for the v2 reproduction**

When `cache is None`, this replacement now omits value scaling entirely. Since every case also compares the full-forward result, the mutant is rejected by that unrelated mismatch even if the grader's cache-state comparison is removed or broken, so the retained calibration does not establish that the cache check detects post-update scaling. Keep the scaling after `update_and_fetch` but outside the cache guard so only the cached values distinguish this control.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Validate every file copied from the pinned checkout**

`verify_baseline()` checks hidden index flags only for `TARGET_PATH`, although `_copy_package()` exports every Python file under `mlx_lm`. If any imported dependency has an assume-unchanged or skip-worktree modification, `git status` remains clean and the target hash still matches, so the supposedly pinned workspace can contain unverified runtime code and its grading result is no longer attributable to the frozen revision. Current candidate export calls `verify_pinned_source_tree()` before copying. The v9 calibration lock covers that verifier and the current public exporter.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Validate hidden Git flags for every v8 input**

When the v8 protocol, lock, or v8-specific implementation files carry `assume-unchanged` or `skip-worktree`, the later `git status` check still reports a clean tree, while this verifier merely compares their mutually editable working-tree hashes. A modified calibration script plus correspondingly modified protocol and lock can therefore pass verification and be retained as evidence under the frozen v8 identity. AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L48-L48](https://github.com/mitukx/VARE/blob/bda97d835f8099f64f96e029f92e1a6ef089008b/AGENTS.md#L48-L48)

V8 is preserved as historical. The current v9 verifier checks `git ls-files -v` for protocol, lock, source manifest, task inputs, and every implementation file, rejecting S/lowercase index tags before calibration or grading. The v9 verifier and tests are hash-locked; no v8 identity was resealed.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Dispatch the public grader to the inventory-enforcing version**

When callers use the unversioned `grade_workspace()` entry point, this still selects v4, whose workspace check validates only the target path and then copies arbitrary Python dependencies supplied in the candidate workspace. Thus a candidate can modify an imported non-target module despite the task's one-file restriction, bypassing the dependency inventory checks added in v7. Publish a newly locked current protocol that routes this entry point through the inventory-enforcing grader.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L48-L48](https://github.com/mitukx/VARE/blob/bda97d835f8099f64f96e029f92e1a6ef089008b/AGENTS.md#L48-L48)

This does not alter v2.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Pin all imported evaluator modules in the v8 inventory**

When v8 is rerun from a later clean commit, this inventory can still verify successfully after unlisted evaluator dependencies change: importing `vare.isolated_candidate` executes `vare/__init__.py` and `_public.py`, while `container_isolation.py` imports the unlisted `attestation.py`, `types.py`, and `evidence.py`. Because neither the implementation hash check nor the clean-worktree check binds those committed files, their import-time code can alter grading behavior while the run is recorded under the frozen v8 identity; include every transitive evaluator module in the locked inventory.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L48-L48](https://github.com/mitukx/VARE/blob/1b6eaadb8f9d7c842819c9fbc37756564ccb07fc/AGENTS.md#L48-L48)

V9 adds the complete local evaluator import set to its independent implementation manifest (`vare.__init__`, `_public`, attestation, container_isolation, evidence, isolated_candidate, types, and task modules), plus the verifier and calibration files. Its protocol lock contains 20 paths and the recorded run binds their hashes.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Verify every historical implementation hash**

This loop deliberately skips 10 of the 12 v5 implementation entries, and the analogous v6 test verifies only one of 14. Because the protocol and lock are mutable files checked only against each other, coordinated corruption of an unchecked evaluator file and both JSON records would still pass these tests while invalidating the claimed historical provenance. Compare every locked path—and preferably the protocol and lock themselves—with blobs from the historical revision.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L48-L48](https://github.com/mitukx/VARE/blob/11cd1ec72cdc228e27f9826cb505919957874333/AGENTS.md#L48-L48)

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Fixed in commit 6329bd4c. Added an auditor for frozen v4–v9 protocol/lock pairs that verifies each protocol and lock byte-for-byte against its recoverable source commit and hashes all 85 declared implementation blobs there. The new regression coherently edits the implementation hash in both worktree JSON files and confirms the frozen Git-source comparison rejects it. Append-only evidence: results/mlxlm-1971-historical-implementation-audit-v1/audit.json; targeted tests, Ruff, mypy, and its SHA manifest pass.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Disable replacement refs when resolving audit commits**

This verification claim is not fail-closed when the repository has a local `refs/replace/<source_commit>` entry: both `git cat-file` and `git show` in the auditor follow the replacement object. With the working protocol, lock, and implementation coherently changed to match a tampered replacement commit, `audit_frozen_pair()` succeeds and records the original source SHA even though it never read that listed object; this is reproducible with `git replace <trusted> <tampered>`. Set `GIT_NO_REPLACE_OBJECTS=1` for every Git subprocess, as the continuation auditor already does, before claiming the pinned objects were verified.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L48-L48](https://github.com/mitukx/VARE/blob/6329bd4cb54185166ae2438e40052aa98faf3db4/AGENTS.md#L48-L48)

Fixed on final HEAD ceee8195: every historical object read (`cat-file` and `show`) sets GIT_NO_REPLACE_OBJECTS=1. Added a git replace regression that redirects the trusted commit to coordinated tampered protocol/lock/implementation bytes and confirms the audit rejects them. Replacement-safe evidence v2 is retained under results/mlxlm-1971-historical-implementation-audit-v2/.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Anchor the v9 lock outside mutable working files**

When the public `grade_workspace()` or `export_candidate()` entrypoint runs from a checkout where the protocol, lock, and evaluator files have been edited coherently, this check still succeeds because it compares only mutually editable working-tree data; unlike the historical auditor, it never compares v9 against the pinned `3f12eef...` Git objects. An altered grader can therefore accept a candidate while still reporting the v9 protocol identity, so the public verification path must validate the frozen protocol, lock, and implementation bytes against an immutable commit before grading.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L48-L48](https://github.com/mitukx/VARE/blob/784b370fd11be7968834204efeae4523ff705c07/AGENTS.md#L48-L48)

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Disable replacement refs in the v9 calibration**

When `HEAD` has a replacement ref to a coherently tampered commit and the index/worktree is reset through that replacement, this `git status` reports clean while the later `rev-parse HEAD` still records the original SHA; the replacement can contain matching altered protocol, lock, and evaluator bytes, so the runner can emit passing evidence under the trusted implementation identity. Set `GIT_NO_REPLACE_OBJECTS=1` on this and the other revision-sensitive v9 Git calls (`show` and `worktree add/remove`), as the historical auditor now does.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L48-L48](https://github.com/mitukx/VARE/blob/784b370fd11be7968834204efeae4523ff705c07/AGENTS.md#L48-L48)

Open the final path with exclusive-create semantics (`"x"`/`O_EXCL`) so the non-overwrite property is enforced atomically rather than by a time-of-check/time-of-use sequence.

nodes.title: Add dual-Python HF Coding Development protocol v2
Preserve attested MLX-LM calibration evidence on publication failure

nodes.body:
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reserve the evidence destination atomically**

When the output parent is writable by another process, the separate `exists()`/`is_symlink()` preflight leaves a race before the pinned child creates the directory. An attacker can insert a symlink to a nonexistent external target during that interval; the legacy child calls `resolve()` and then creates and writes the target, potentially returning success while the requested output remains a retargetable symlink. Reserve and validate the destination atomically so redirected or raced output fails closed.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L48-L52](https://github.com/mitukx/VARE/blob/45fd0da592955205e6518c12e9e9b315797541e2/AGENTS.md#L48-L52)

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

Proposed correction in 3ff93739: one exclusive mkdir reserves output at mode 0700 before worktree/child execution, with an operator-owned parent that rejects group/world write access. Child raw evidence goes to the absent records/ leaf, and reservation inode/type is checked before and after child execution. A regression attempts symlink insertion at child launch and confirms rejection and retention of negative child records; existing outputs cannot be reused. The ancestor namespace and same-UID processes remain explicitly operator-controlled. Please independently reassess this correction; leaving this P1 open pending review, particularly namespace assumptions. No calibration/model inference ran.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve symlink identity for the pinned exporter**

When `run_pinned_v9_task("export", ...)` receives a symlinked source checkout or patch, resolving these arguments here converts them into ordinary target paths before the pinned v9 code sees them. This bypasses the historical exporter's explicit rejection of a symlinked source root and symlinked patch, so an export can be accepted under inputs that the frozen protocol deliberately rejects. Reject symlinks before canonicalization or pass the original absolute paths to the pinned validator.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L72-L72](https://github.com/mitukx/VARE/blob/45fd0da592955205e6518c12e9e9b315797541e2/AGENTS.md#L72-L72)

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

Addressed in new head 3ff93739: source, patch and workspace paths (including ancestors) reject symlinks before canonicalization/dispatch. Export snapshots a bounded regular patch via O_NOFOLLOW before creating the pinned worktree; the child's validate/apply/hash uses the private read-only copy even if the caller later replaces the original. New regressions failed before the fix; operator plus immutable-attestation tests now pass 20/20. Ruff, mypy and diff check pass. This does not change #117's historical 45fd0da pin or frozen v9.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Disable Git hooks before adding the worktree**

When the repository or operator's Git configuration sets `core.hooksPath`, this command executes its `post-checkout` hook before `attest_current_v9` runs; the same exposure exists in the calibration call above. Git explicitly documents that `post-checkout` runs for `git worktree add` unless `--no-checkout` is used ([githooks documentation](https://git-scm.com/docs/githooks#_post_checkout)), and I reproduced it with Git 2.43 despite `GIT_NO_REPLACE_OBJECTS=1`. Thus mutable, unattested configuration can execute arbitrary operator-privileged code and alter external inputs or evidence before attestation, so these Git invocations need a hook-disabled/sanitized configuration rather than inheriting `os.environ` and repository config.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L48-L48](https://github.com/mitukx/VARE/blob/3ff937397164027b5ec4fc226cea411c97666980/AGENTS.md#L48-L48)

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

Addressed in c5b52a4a. Both operator paths now discard ambient GIT_* routing/config overrides, disable system/global config, and inherit command-scope core.hooksPath=/dev/null and core.fsmonitor=false through the pinned historical child. A real tiny Git fixture first confirms its configured post-checkout hook executes, then verifies run_frozen_calibration does not execute it despite injected GIT_DIR and GIT_CONFIG_COUNT overrides. No model/Docker calibration runs in the fixture. Focused operator/attestation suite: 21 passed; Ruff/mypy/diff check passed. This is a scoped hook/routing fix, not a complete certification of arbitrary local Git filters. #117's old pin is unchanged.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve staged records when cross-filesystem publication fails**

When the requested output is on a different filesystem from the default temporary directory, this rename raises `EXDEV`, and the enclosing `TemporaryDirectory` cleanup then deletes the only copy of the raw records. This affects successful and failed children alike, leaving an empty reserved output instead of recoverable evidence. I reproduced this with staging under `/tmp` and an operator-owned output parent under `/dev/shm`: a child returning 1 wrote `failure.json`, publication failed, and the staged records were deleted. Stage records on the destination filesystem while preserving descriptor-relative publication, or retain a durable recovery location whenever publication fails.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L52-L52](https://github.com/mitukx/VARE/blob/2e463441e158342efabf60ee7743b01c102e0f59/AGENTS.md#L52-L52)

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

Fixed in `38eaf6dce670d5d8be0fcecc99cbcd35491aee0e`: raw records stage in a fresh mode-0700 directory under the reserved output's parent, so normal publication stays on the same filesystem. If publication still errors, the error reports the retained staging path and the code leaves those files in place. A regression injects EXDEV at the rename and confirms the failure record remains. Focused suite: 16 passed; Ruff, mypy, and diff check passed. Please recheck the exact head.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Apply the sanitized Git environment during attestation**

When ambient Git configuration defines an executable `core.fsmonitor`, this in-process attestation bypasses `_git_environment()`: its Git calls use `GIT_ENV` from `audit_mlxlm_1971_historical_implementation_hashes.py`, which retains the original environment and global configuration. Fresh evidence at this exact head: with Git 2.43, an ambient fsmonitor script executed during the real attestation despite the sanitized worktree commands; only the subsequent calibration child was mocked. Git documents this setting as the pathname of the [“fsmonitor” hook command](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-config/2.43.0#Documentation/git-config.txt-corefsmonitor). Because `attest_current_v9` runs `ls-files` after checking evaluator bytes, that command can modify already-verified files before dispatch without another byte check. Pass the sanitized environment through every attestation Git call in both operator paths, rather than only worktree creation and child execution.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L48-L48](https://github.com/mitukx/VARE/blob/38eaf6dce670d5d8be0fcecc99cbcd35491aee0e/AGENTS.md#L48-L48)

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

The attestation environment is sanitized in the current PR head. `audit_mlxlm_1971_historical_implementation_hashes.py::_git_environment()` removes all inherited `GIT_*` variables, disables system/global config, sets `GIT_NO_REPLACE_OBJECTS=1`, and applies command-scope `core.fsmonitor=false`; `GIT_ENV` is used by `audit_frozen_pair`, `_git_bytes`, and the attestation `ls-files` call. The regression `test_v9_attestation_disables_repository_fsmonitor` proves the local-config hook runs in an unsanitized positive control and does not run during attestation. I ran that test and `test_operator_disables_real_configured_checkout_hook_and_ambient_git_routes` on the current descendant; both pass. Please recheck the current PR head `8257a4dfe2106055a048ddd4b1520a08c7e4d658` and resolve this thread if the fix is confirmed.

nodes.title: Isolate MLX-LM source snapshots before trusted export

nodes.body:
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Disable repository hooks before staging trusted code**

When the repository has an attacker-controlled `post-checkout` hook, including one selected through `core.hooksPath`, this command executes it inside the new worktree; the [Git hook documentation](https://git-scm.com/docs/githooks) confirms that `post-checkout` runs after `git worktree add` unless `--no-checkout` is used. The hook can add an untracked `scripts/__init__.py` or crafted bytecode, neither of which is covered by `PINNED_OPERATOR_SOURCES`, so the `-I` child can execute attacker code and emit forged passing evidence while all three checked source files still match Git. Disable hooks and untrusted Git configuration during both worktree checkouts and reject extra import artifacts before launching Python.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L48-L48](https://github.com/mitukx/VARE/blob/2c1109b141ed469e3de84fe9a8011663a937fff7/AGENTS.md#L48-L48)

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

Addressed on `316f89011d9a94b9df7a9218fec617ac37d2dc20`: the trusted worktree is now added with `--no-checkout`; sparse checkout and `read-tree -mu` materialize the selected trusted paths without invoking `post-checkout`. The real temporary-repository regression configures a malicious local `core.hooksPath` and verifies the hook marker is never created. The 56-test focused suite passes.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Validate the child evidence schema before returning it**

If the pinned subprocess returns a syntactically valid but incomplete object such as `{"passed": true}`, this check accepts it and the CLI exits successfully; the new dispatch test even treats `{"passed": false}` alone as valid. **<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve missing-newline boundaries in generated diffs**

When an allowlisted file has no trailing newline, `splitlines(keepends=True)` leaves its final line unterminated and `"".join(...)` concatenates the deletion and addition into a single hunk line such as `-one+two`. The function nevertheless returns `applied: true` and hashes this malformed diff, so the retained output cannot reliably represent or replay the applied edit; generate explicit no-newline markers or otherwise validate the diff before reporting success.

When `root` is something like `alias/workspace` and `alias` is a symlink, `root.is_symlink()` is false and the subsequent component walk starts below that alias, so reads and `os.replace` operate through the symlink even without a concurrent writer. nodes.title: Measure deterministic edit replay and recovery; pin E2E inventories
Add bounded source navigation for repair agents

nodes.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Bound the path inventory independently of search results**

When the allowlist contains many moderately long paths, `indexed_paths` alone exceeds the response budget, and `_bounded()` discards every match before returning `output_limit_too_small`. I reproduced this with 128 valid source paths of 116 characters each under the default 8 KiB limit: indexing succeeds, but every search fails regardless of query. Truncate or omit the path inventory independently so that supported source sets still return useful bounded search results.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Retry index construction after a recoverable build failure**

If a source temporarily exceeds an index limit or becomes unreadable, the failed rebuild clears the snapshot and sets `_last_build_error`; this early return then prevents all subsequent freshness checks and rebuilds, even after the source is repaired. I reproduced this by exceeding the per-file line limit, searching once, restoring a valid two-line file, and searching again: the navigator permanently reports the old limit error. Retry a bounded rebuild on subsequent searches so a recoverable source problem does not disable navigation for the remainder of the repair session.
